newsitem.title: AFGHANISTAN: Taleban say they repel opposition attack in north.
newsitem.headline: Taleban say they repel opposition attack in north.

text.p: The Taleban Islamic militia repulsed an attack on their positions south of the town of Aibak on Saturday, a senior Taleban official said.

"The opposition launched an offensive at 7.00 a.m. (0230 GMT). They were beaten back and their dead bodies and burnt vehicles are still on the front line. One Taleban fighter counted more than 50 bodies," Taleban Information Minister Amir Khan Mutaqi told reporters in Pul-i-Khumri.
He said the front line was some 50 km (31 miles) north of the town of Pul-i-Khumri, just south of Aibak, capital of Samangan province.
Opposition forces were shelling Taleban positions behind the front line when journalists visited the area on Saturday morning. It was not possible to reach the front line.
Mutaqi said the Taleban had formed a new front line on the borders of the northwestern provinces of Badghis and Faryab.
"The front line is on the border of Badgis and Faryab provinces. Badghis is entirely in our hands," he said.

The Taleban took four nothern provinces last week when one opposition Uzbek commander, General Abdul Malik, apparently defected to them. They were forced to relinquish their gains when their erstwhile ally turned on them.
They were driven out of the city of Mazar-i-Sharif, the opposition capital and the most important town in northern Afghanistan, after fierce street battles on Wednesday.
The International Committee of the Red Cross said they had picked up over 100 bodies from the streets of Mazar-i-Sharif.
Mutaqi said he had no information about the Taleban forces who had been driven out of Mazar-i-Sharif.
Mutaqi said the strategically vital road from Kabul to northern Afghanistan was open again on Saturday morning after heavy fighting on Friday when the opposition took the town of Jabal-os-Seraj.
The town lies astride the road as it enters the Hindu Kush mountain range, some 70 km (56 miles) north of Kabul.

"The road is in full control of the Taleban forces. Yesterday the opposition launched a heavy offesnive against us in Jabal-os-Seraj and took the town. When we counter-attacked we retook it and killed many of their fighters," he said.
There was no independent confirmation of his account.
Mutaqi said the road was open for traffic on Saturday, but although there was traffic moving south of Jabal-os-Seraj, there was no sign of traffic coming north from Kabul.
